newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian farmers reject drought review.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian farmers reject drought review.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers Federation (NFF) on Tuesday rejected an official Australian and New Zealand proposal to abolish special government relief in droughts.

A drought policy review task force, set up by the Agriculture and Resource Management Council of Australia and New Zealand, sought to abolish relief based on exceptional circumstances and instead set up a new farm savings scheme.

But the NFF's farm business management committee said the task force's proposal to abolish the provisions was unacceptable to the farm sector, because farmers could not adequately prepare for such circumstances.

"NFF wants to move away from the notion that exceptional circumstances can exist as part of farmers contingency plans, and (that) this is likely to follow the increasing adoption of property management plans and better risk management," committee chairman Ian Macfarlane told the NFF's annual conference.
Macfarlane said the government should recognise that exceptional circumstances had devastating impacts on the industry, the community and the economy.
The review's proposed farm savings scheme would be an unattractive solution to the problem, he said.
"It would seem much less confusing and much more attractive to streamline any farm savings vehicles into one product available through financial institutions," he said.
But the NFF supported some of the review's proposals, including the need for more emphasis on education and training to develop risk management skills, he said.
